headline_marked: AQI 234: [[Dhaka ranks first globally]] in air pollution
headline: AQI 234: Dhaka ranks first globally in air pollution
summary: The capital's air quality was categorized as 'very unhealthy' on Tuesday morning, surpassing other major cities like Kolkata and Kuala Lumpur.
details: According to IQAir, Dhaka's Air Quality Index (AQI) reached 234 on Tuesday morning, making it the most polluted city in the world at that time.
The city's air was categorized as 'very unhealthy,' with Kolkata (198), Kuala Lumpur (191), and Delhi (186) following in the rankings.
The primary pollutant was PM2.5, with a concentration of 159 micrograms per cubic meter, which is approximately 32 times the WHO's annual guideline value.
Several monitoring stations in Dhaka recorded severe levels, with Baridhara Park Road topping the list at 284, followed by BIDS and Gulshan Lake Park at 273.
Other affected areas including Becharam Deuri, Sagupta, and South Pallabi also reported 'very unhealthy' air quality levels.
Similar hazardous conditions were noted in surrounding areas, with Gazipur recording an AQI of 245 and Tongi at 185.
IQAir notes that these indices are real-time and subject to change as atmospheric conditions shift throughout the day.
caption:
Dhaka is currently the most polluted city on Earth. The air we breathe is 32 times over the WHO limit.

According to IQAir, Dhaka's Air Quality Index (AQI) reached 234 on Tuesday morning, making it the most polluted city in the world at that time.

The city's air was categorized as 'very unhealthy,' with Kolkata (198), Kuala Lumpur (191), and Delhi (186) following in the rankings.

The primary pollutant was PM2.5, with a concentration of 159 micrograms per cubic meter, which is approximately 32 times the WHO's annual guideline value.

Several monitoring stations in Dhaka recorded severe levels, with Baridhara Park Road topping the list at 284, followed by BIDS and Gulshan Lake Park at 273.

Other affected areas including Becharam Deuri, Sagupta, and South Pallabi also reported 'very unhealthy' air quality levels.

Similar hazardous conditions were noted in surrounding areas, with Gazipur recording an AQI of 245 and Tongi at 185.

IQAir notes that these indices are real-time and subject to change as atmospheric conditions shift throughout the day.

headline_marked: 447 [[arrested in Dhaka in a day]] during police operations
headline: 447 arrested in Dhaka in a day during police operations
summary: Dhaka Metropolitan Police conducted raids across the city, filing 58 cases and seizing narcotics, weapons, and cash.
details: Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) arrested 447 people in regular operations across the capital over a 24-hour period. The police filed 58 cases against the arrestees.
The operations were carried out by personnel from various police stations. The Mirpur Division led with 101 arrests, followed by Tejgaon with 70, Motijheel with 67, and Wari with 56.
Other arrests were made in the Lalbagh (47), Uttara (47), Gulshan (29), and Ramna (27) divisions, while the Detective Branch arrested three people.
Police seized 51.5kg of marijuana, 1,000 pieces of yaba, 51 packs of heroin, 19 bottles of phensedyl, two machetes, three knives, Tk 16,200 in cash, and two mobile phones.
The DMP stated that further legal action against those arrested is currently being processed.
caption:
447 people arrested in just 24 hours. Police raids across Dhaka lead to massive narcotics and weapon seizures.

Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) arrested 447 people in regular operations across the capital over a 24-hour period. The police filed 58 cases against the arrestees.

The operations were carried out by personnel from various police stations. The Mirpur Division led with 101 arrests, followed by Tejgaon with 70, Motijheel with 67, and Wari with 56.

Other arrests were made in the Lalbagh (47), Uttara (47), Gulshan (29), and Ramna (27) divisions, while the Detective Branch arrested three people.

Police seized 51.5kg of marijuana, 1,000 pieces of yaba, 51 packs of heroin, 19 bottles of phensedyl, two machetes, three knives, Tk 16,200 in cash, and two mobile phones.

The DMP stated that further legal action against those arrested is currently being processed.
